322013.title: The locally conical reflection arrangement conjecture
322013.statement:
Let $W$ be a well-generated reflection group acting on a complex vector space $V$. A generating set $R$ is **well-generating** when it generates $W$ and has cardinality $\dim V$. The system $(W,R)$ is called **abstractly locally conical** if, for every $U,T\subseteq R$ with $U$ nonempty, every Quillen fiber of

$$
\mathrm{Supp}:\mathrm{Face}(\Delta^U_T)\to \Pi^U_T\setminus\{\hat{1}\}
$$

has a cone point. **The locally conical reflection arrangement conjecture.** For each well-generated reflection group $W$, there exists a well-generating $R$ for which $(W,R)$ is abstractly locally conical. This property would provide the local conical structure needed to compare the relevant simplicial complexes with the intersection lattice of the reflection arrangement; whether every well-generated reflection group admits such a generating set is left open.

319799.title: Ackerman's linear extremal conjecture for forbidden circle-graph matchings
319799.statement: A **geometric graph** is a graph drawn in the plane with vertices represented by points and edges as straight-line segments. A **circle graph** $F$ is the intersection graph of chords on a circle. A matching in a geometric graph has an intersection graph whose vertices correspond to the matching edges, with adjacency when the corresponding edges cross. **Ackerman's linear extremal conjecture for forbidden circle-graph matchings.** For any circle graph $F$ on $k$ vertices, there exists a constant $c_k$ such that every $n$-vertex geometric graph that does not contain a matching whose intersection graph is $F$ contains at most $c_kn$ edges. This extends the paper's established linear bound for the relevant three-vertex case and would give a uniform linear extremal bound for every fixed circle graph. The general assertion is presented as a conjecture and no resolution is supplied here.

320610.title: Finiteness conjecture for non-singular unsatisfiable hitting clause-sets
320610.statement:
A clause-set is **hitting** if every two distinct clauses $C,C'$ clash in at least one variable, that is, $\lvert C\cap\overline{C'}\rvert\geq 1$. A clause-set is **non-singular** in the sense used in the paper, and its **deficiency** is denoted by $k\in\mathbb{N}$. Two clause-sets have the same isomorphism type when they are isomorphic under the relevant variable and clause structure.

**Finiteness conjecture.** For every deficiency $k\in\mathbb{N}$, there are only finitely many isomorphism types of non-singular unsatisfiable hitting clause-sets.

This is presented as the main conjecture motivating the classification of minimally unsatisfiable clause-sets by deficiency, especially the classification of unsatisfiable hitting clause-sets. The supplied text gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

320804.title: The product conjecture for finite transitive sets
320804.statement:
Let $X\subset\mathbb R^m$ be a finite transitive set. A finite set $Y\subset\mathbb R^d$ is **$k$-Ramsey for $X$** if every $k$-colouring of $Y$ contains a monochromatic subset congruent to $X$. For a positive integer $n$, regard $X^n$ as a subset of $\mathbb R^{mn}$, and call a scalar multiple of it a **scaling** of $X^n$.

**Product conjecture.** For every positive integer $k$, there exists a positive integer $n$ such that some scaling of $X^n$ is $k$-Ramsey for $X$.

This is a stronger formulation of the transitive-set characterization: it would immediately imply the “if” direction. It abstracts the product-and-scaling constructions used in known proofs that particular sets are Ramsey. The paper states that it is equivalent to the main transitive-set conjecture, but does not establish it.

320805.title: The block-permutation conjecture
320805.statement:
For positive integers $m$ and $n$, let $[m]=\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ and let $[m]^n$ denote the words of length $n$ over $[m]$. A **block permutation set** in $[m]^n$ is obtained by choosing pairwise disjoint blocks $I_1,\ldots,I_m\subset[n]$, fixing all coordinates outside their union, and taking all words obtained by assigning a permutation of $1,\ldots,m$ to the blocks. Its **degree** is $\sum_{j=1}^m|I_j|$.

**Block-permutation conjecture.** For every pair of positive integers $m$ and $k$, there exist positive integers $n$ and $d$ such that every $k$-colouring of $[m]^n$ contains a block permutation set of degree $d$.

This is the fixed-block-size Hales--Jewett-type formulation arising from the group-action conjecture. It asks for a monochromatic family containing all permutations of the alphabet across prescribed blocks; the paper presents it as a conjectural combinatorial reformulation.

320911.title: Polar-dual Neumann eigenvalue sum conjecture for convex domains
320911.statement:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a bounded convex domain containing the origin. Write $\mu_j$ for its Neumann Laplace eigenvalues, $V$ for volume, $I$ for the moment of inertia, and $\Omega^\circ$ for the polar dual of $\Omega$, defined by

$$
\Omega^\circ=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d:x\cdot y<1\text{ for all }y\in\overline{\Omega}\}.
$$

**Polar-dual Neumann eigenvalue sum conjecture.** The scale-invariant quantity

$$
\left.(\mu_2+\dots+\mu_n)V^{2/d}\right|_\Omega\left.\frac{V^{1+2/d}}{I}\right|_{\Omega^\circ}
$$

is maximal when $\Omega$ is a ball, for each $n\geq2$.
This conjecture proposes the maximizer for the Neumann analogue of a bounded polar-dual eigenvalue expression; the corresponding Dirichlet quantity is bounded above using John’s ellipsoid theorem, but the maximizing statement for general convex domains is presented as an open problem.

318150.title: Sun's Lucas and mixed Fibonacci–Lucas representation conjectures
318150.statement: Let $F_n$ and $L_n$ denote the Fibonacci and Lucas sequences, respectively. A sequence term is **positive** when its value is positive, and a term is **odd** when it is not divisible by $2$. **Sun's Lucas and mixed Fibonacci–Lucas conjectures.** (i) Every integer $n>4$ can be written as the sum of an odd prime, an odd Lucas number, and a positive Lucas number. For $k=2,3$, every integer $n>4$ can be written as $p+L_s+L_t^k$, where $p$ is an odd prime, $s,t\geqslant0$, and $L_s$ or $L_t$ is odd. (ii) Every integer $n>4$ can be written as the sum of an odd prime, a positive Fibonacci number, and twice a positive Fibonacci number, or half of a positive Fibonacci number. Also, every integer $n>4$ can be written as the sum of an odd prime, twice a positive Fibonacci number, and the square of a positive Fibonacci number. (iii) Every integer $n>4$ can be written as $p+F_s+L_t$, where $p$ is an odd prime, $s>0$, and $F_s$ or $L_t$ is odd. The source reports extensive computational checks, but these assertions remain open.

318395.title: Linear-equations conjecture for d-refined alternating sign matrix enumeration
318395.statement:
For $1\le d<n$ and $1\le i_1<i_2<\cdots<i_d\le n$, let $A_{n,i_1,i_2,\ldots,i_d}$ be the number of monotone triangles of order $n-d$ whose bottom row is the increasing arrangement of $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}\setminus\{i_1,i_2,\ldots,i_d\}$; when $d=n$, set $A_{n,1,2,\ldots,n}=1$. Extend these values to an array $(\hat{A}_{n,i_1,\ldots,i_d})_{1\le i_1,\ldots,i_d\le n}$.

**Linear-equations conjecture.** The extension can be chosen so that, for $1\le i_1,i_2,\ldots,i_d\le n$,

$$
\hat{A}_{n,i_1,\ldots,i_d}=(-1)^{nd}\sum_{j_1=i_1}^n\cdots\sum_{j_d=i_d}^n(-1)^{j_1+\cdots+j_d}\prod_{r=1}^d\binom{2n-i_r-d}{j_r-i_r}\hat{A}_{n,j_d,\ldots,j_2,j_1}.
$$

This extends the linear relations for doubly refined enumeration to arbitrary refinement degree $d$. The source presents it as conjectural; no resolution evidence is supplied.

317029.title: The existence conjecture for $k$-symmetric permutations

317510.title: The level partial-field universality conjecture
317510.statement:
Let ${\mathbb{P}}$ be a partial field, and let ${\cal M}$ be a class of matroids. Say that ${\mathbb{P}}$ is ${\cal M}$-universal if, for every partial field ${\mathbb{P}}'$ such that every matroid in ${\cal M}$ is ${\mathbb{P}}'$-representable, there exists a homomorphism ${\mathbb{P}}\rightarrow {\mathbb{P}}'$. Then ${\mathbb{P}}$ is ${\cal M}$-universal.

This conjecture asks whether every level partial field is universal for precisely the class of matroids it represents. The source presents it as an open question in the discussion of universal and level partial fields.

317936.title: The Lefschetz condition conjecture for Braden–MacPherson sheaves
317936.statement:

$$

(\operatorname{coker}f)_{\{l-n\}}\stackrel{\sim}{\to}(\operatorname{coker}f)_{\{l+n\}}

for every $n\ge1$. **The Lefschetz condition conjecture.** For all $x\le w$, the map $i_x$ satisfies the Lefschetz condition with center $l(w)$. 379793.title: Quantum determinant–permanent reciprocity conjecture
379793.statement:

m_q^\lambda(\alpha(q))_{\mathrm{per}}=m_q^{\lambda'}(\alpha(q^{-1})).

379797.title: Span-intersection conjecture for upper and lower roots
379797.statement:
Let $W$ be a finite Coxeter group of rank $n$, let $c$ be a Coxeter element, and let $(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_k,\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_{n-k})$ be a $c$-cluster, where the $\alpha_i$ are its lower roots and the $\beta_i$ are its upper roots. Let $\phi_c$ be the recursively defined map on roots, and write $\beta_i^{\perp}$ for the hyperplane orthogonal to $\beta_i$. **Span-intersection conjecture.** One has

$$

378963.title: Structural conjecture for sumsets bounded by a fixed multiple of the set size
378963.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a real number satisfying

$$
3<\alpha<3+\frac{1}{3},
$$

and let $A\subseteq\mathbb N$ be finite. Write $2A=A+A=\{a+a':a,a'\in A\}$ and set $b=|2A|-3|A|+3$. An **arithmetic progression** is a finite set of equally spaced integers, and a **bi-progression** is the structured object used in the source's additive-combinatorial results.

$$
3|A|-3\leqslant |2A|=3|A|-3+b\leqslant\alpha|A|,
$$

then $A$ is either a subset of an arithmetic progression of length at most $2|A|-1+2b$ or a subset of a bi-progression of length at most $|A|+b$.

379094.title: The extremal configuration conjecture for the $pi$-pebbling function
379094.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $p_i$ denote the pebbling demand associated with vertex $i$, and let $pi^{t}(G)=k$. A configuration assigns $c_i$ pebbles to each vertex, and it is **non-$t$-solvable** if it cannot be pebbled to a configuration satisfying the relevant $t$-pebbling requirement. For the standard price function, $r$ should have another vertex $s$ at distance $d$ from it, and there should be a shortest path from $r$ to such an $s$ containing no pebbles other than those on $r$.

379147.title: Sundaram–Welker vanishing conjecture for polynomial root-multiplicity strata
379147.statement:

$$

$$

$$

**Monotonicity conjecture.** If the integer triplet $(n,d,k)$ is accurate, then the integer triplet $(n',d',k')$ is also accurate whenever $n'\geq n$, $d'\leq d$, and $k'\leq k$.
This conjecture asserts monotonicity of accuracy under more boxes, fewer steps, and smaller query size. The supplied text gives no evidence that it has been resolved.

373645.statement:

$$

$$
\#\{m\in B_k:F(m)=r\}=2^{k-r+2}\qquad(3\le r\le k+1),

$$
\#\{m\in B_k:F(m)=k+2\}=1,\qquad \#\{m\in B_k:F(m)=k+3\}=1.

315939.title: Nagata–Biran conjecture
315939.statement:
Let $X$ be a smooth complex projective surface and let $L$ be an ample line
bundle on $X$, and write $d=\sqrt{L^{2}}$ for its degree, where $L^{2}=L\cdot L$
denotes the self-intersection number. For points $p_{1},\ldots,p_{r}\in X$ the
multi-point Seshadri constant of $L$ is

$$
\varepsilon(p_{1},\ldots,p_{r};X,L)=\inf_{C}\frac{L\cdot C}{\sum_{i=1}^{r}\operatorname{mult}_{p_{i}}C},
$$

the infimum being taken over all irreducible curves $C\subset X$ with
$\sum_{i=1}^{r}\operatorname{mult}_{p_{i}}C>0$, where $\operatorname{mult}_{p}C$
is the multiplicity of $C$ at $p$.

Then there exists an integer $r_{0}=r_{0}(X,L)$ such that for every $r\ge
r_{0}$ and every choice of very general points $p_{1},\ldots,p_{r}\in X$,

$$
\varepsilon(p_{1},\ldots,p_{r};X,L)=\frac{d}{\sqrt{r}}.
$$

315961.title: filling area conjecture
315961.statement:
Let
$M$ be a compact orientable smooth surface with nonempty boundary, equipped with a Riemannian metric, and let $C=\partial
M$. Regard $M$ and
$C$ as metric spaces with their intrinsic distances: for $x,y\in M$, $d_M(x,y)$
is the infimum of the lengths of paths in $M$ from $x$ to $y$, and for $x,y\in
C$, $d_C(x,y)$ is the infimum of the lengths of paths in $C$ from $x$ to
$y$. Assume that $C$ is a closed curve of length $2L$ with $L>0$, and that
$M$ fills $C$ isometrically, i.e.

$$
d_M(x,y)=d_C(x,y)\qquad\text{for all }x,y\in C.
$$

Then

$$
\operatorname{area}(M)\;\ge\;\frac{2L^{2}}{\pi},
$$

the area of a round hemisphere whose boundary circle has length $2L$.

315992.title: Brouwer's conjecture
315992.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple undirected graph on $n$ vertices with
$m(G)$ edges, let $A(G)$ be its adjacency matrix, let
$D(G)$ be the diagonal matrix of its vertex degrees, and let $L(G) = D(G) -
A(G)$ be its Laplacian matrix. Denote the eigenvalues of $L(G)$ by

$$
\lambda_n(L(G)) \leq \lambda_{n-1}(L(G)) \leq \cdots \leq \lambda_1(L(G)).
$$

Then for every $t \in \{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$,

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{t} \lambda_i(L(G)) \leq m(G) + \binom{t+1}{2}.
$$
